title: Tobacco (Control of Advertisements and Sale) (Amendment) Bill
what_it_is: Tobacco (Control of Advertisements and Sale) (Amendment) Bill

sections.label: Smoking deaths and falling rates
sections.summary: About six Singaporeans die prematurely daily from smoking-related diseases, while smoking rates fell from 18.3% in 1992 to 12.6% in 2004.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: About six Singaporeans die prematurely from smoking-related diseases each day.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: In Singapore, we have brought down smoking rates over the years, from 18.3% in 1992, to an all-time low of 12.6% in 2004.

sections.label: Smoking prevalence creeping up
sections.summary: Smoking prevalence has crept up in recent years to reach 13.3% in 2013.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: Nonetheless, our smoking prevalence has, in recent years, crept up somewhat, to reach 13.3% in 2013.

sections.label: Point-of-sale display ban bill
sections.summary: The Tobacco (Control of Advertisements and Sale) (Amendment) Bill seeks to amend the Act to introduce the point-of-sale display ban.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: The Tobacco (Control of Advertisements and Sale) (Amendment) Bill seeks to amend the current Tobacco (Control of Advertisements and Sale) Act to introduce the point-of-sale display ban.

sections.label: Ban extends to components
sections.summary: The ban will extend to components of such products to prevent import in parts and re-assembly.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: The ban will also extend to the components of such products, to prevent such products from being imported in parts and re-assembled thereafter.

sections.label: Electronic advertisement ban extended
sections.summary: Clause 4 amends section 3 so the ban on tobacco product advertisements extends to advertisements published electronically in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: Clause 4 of the Bill amends section 3 of the Act such that our ban on tobacco product advertisements extends to advertisements that are published electronically in Singapore.

sections.label: Tobacco loyalty programmes disallowed
sections.summary: New section 9A in clause 10 makes explicit that customer loyalty programmes involving tobacco products and other promotional schemes are disallowed.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: The new section 9A in clause 10 of the Bill makes it explicit that customer loyalty programmes involving tobacco products, such as the redemption of reward points for tobacco products, and other promotional schemes are disallowed.

sections.label: Tobacco licensing and single point of sale
sections.summary: Clause 20 repeals and re-enacts section 18 to clarify tobacco licensing and limit sales to a single point of sale.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: Clause 20 repeals and re-enacts section 18 to clarify the licensing requirements for the wholesale or retail of tobacco products in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: It will limit the sale of tobacco products to a single point of sale specified in the tobacco retail licence, to limit access to tobacco products.

sections.label: Tobacco deaths in Singapore
sections.summary: HPB statistics from May 2015 state tobacco kills about 2,500 smokers and 250 non-smokers yearly in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In Singapore, tobacco kills about 2,500 smokers and 250 non-smokers each year, said the Health Promotion Board (HPB) statistics in May 2015 and that is seven and a half people killed each day.

sections.label: Hidden tobacco display reduces smoking intention
sections.summary: Results published in November last year showed an 11% reduction in smoking intention when tobacco products were hidden.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The results, published in November last year, showed that there was an 11% reduction in smoking intention when the display of tobacco products was hidden, compared to when it was visible behind the cashier.

sections.label: Minimum age and impulsive buys
sections.summary: With a proposed increase in minimum purchase age, the measure is expected to reduce temptation and impulsive cigarette buys.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In conjunction with the proposed increase in the minimum age to purchase cigarettes in the near future, this measure is expected to reduce temptation and impulsive cigarette buys.

sections.label: Expanding to whole Nee Soon South
sections.summary: Following residents' requests, the measures are now being expanded to the whole Nee Soon South.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Following residents' requests, we are now expanding them to the whole Nee Soon South.

sections.label: Resident on stopping smoking
sections.summary: A resident said her lungs are already black and cited an HPB flyer saying 17 days without smoking frees lungs of most toxins.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Because she says that, "Since my lungs are already so black, it does not matter".

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: And she says that one day she saw a flyer from HPB to show them that if you were to stop smoking for a certain number of days – she told me 17 days but when I go and check the website, it has various pages – she says that if she stops smoking for 17 days, her lungs will be free of most toxins.

sections.label: Quitting smoking at 27
sections.summary: She eventually managed to quit smoking at the age of 27.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Eventually, she managed to quit at the age of 27.

sections.label: Small business owners changing focus
sections.summary: It would be impractical to expect small business owners to change their focus quickly, especially since alcohol sales are already restricted.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: It would be impractical to expect these small business owners to change their focus to something else in a short period of time.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: This is especially so since their other major source of revenue, alcohol sales, has been restricted already.

sections.label: Small retailers facing financial difficulties
sections.summary: Many small retailers affected by alcohol restrictions may face financial difficulties as tobacco sales also fall.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: On the other hand, many small retailers are already affected by the restrictions on selling alcohol; now, with tobacco sales also falling, they may face financial difficulties.

sections.label: Smoking death rates and lung cancer
sections.summary: Occasional male smokers have a 1.6 times higher death rate, nearly 1,400 Singaporeans were diagnosed with lung cancer yearly from 2010 to 2014, and six to seven die prematurely daily from smoking-related diseases.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Even men who smoke occasionally have an overall death rate 1.6 times higher than non-smokers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Between 2010 and 2014, there was an average of nearly 1,400 people in Singapore diagnosed with lung cancer each year.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Six to seven Singaporeans die prematurely from smoking-related diseases each day.

sections.label: Tobacco-Free Generation idea
sections.summary: This is key to long-term tobacco control in Singapore and the idea behind campaigns such as Tobacco-Free Generation, where anyone born after a certain date should not buy cigarettes or tobacco.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: And this is the key, Mdm Speaker, to long-term control of tobacco in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: This is the idea behind campaigns, such as those for a Tobacco-Free Generation: the idea that anyone born after a certain date should not be allowed to buy cigarettes or tobacco.

sections.label: Banning point-of-sale display
sections.summary: Passing this Bill will join 16 other overseas jurisdictions in banning point-of-sale display, including Iceland, Russia, Kosovo and Canada.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: When we pass this Bill, we will join 16 other overseas jurisdictions in banning point-of-sale display, which include Iceland, Russia, Kosovo, Canada and the like.

sections.label: Retailers 12-month grace period
sections.summary: Retailers get a 12-month grace period for compliance under the Bill, which the speaker finds possibly too long given smoking's effects.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Third, retailers have been given a 12-month grace period with the passing of this Bill, for compliance.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: I feel that this may be a little too long, considering the magnitude and the multiplier effect of smoking and tobacco, even one extra day is a day too long.

sections.label: Smoker proportion 1992 to 2013
sections.summary: From 1992 to 2013, the proportion of smokers in the community fell by only 5%, from 30.8% to 25.3%.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: From 1992 to 2013, the proportion of smokers in our community went down by only 5%, from 30.8% to 25.3%.

sections.label: New section 12A tobacco display ban
sections.summary: The speaker finds new section 12A, which prohibits display of tobacco products, extremely useful.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: As such, I find the new section 12A, which prohibits the display of tobacco products, extremely useful.

sections.label: Smoking before age 21
sections.summary: The speaker started smoking at 18, and WHO research shows those who do not smoke before 21 are unlikely to start.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I started smoking when I was 18 years old – pretty stressed in school.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: But a research by WHO shows that people who do not pick up smoking before the age of 21 are unlikely to ever start smoking.

sections.label: Singapore resident smoker percentages
sections.summary: Among Singapore residents, current smokers dropped from 18.3% in 1992 to 12.6% in 2004, then stabilised at 13.3% in 2013.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Among Singapore residents, as we have heard earlier, the percentage of current smokers dropped from 18.3% in 1992 to 12.6% in 2004, but stabilised thereafter with 13.3% of smokers in 2013.

sections.label: I Quit campaign pledges
sections.summary: From the "I Quit" campaign's inception to 2014, 5,000 smokers pledged and 14% of them successfully quit.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Since that "I Quit" campaign's inception to 2014, a total of 5,000 smokers have pledged and 14% of those who pledged have successfully quit smoking.

sections.label: 2012 anti-smoking campaign statistics
sections.summary: The 2012 campaign led an estimated 1.64 million Americans to try quitting, with about 100,000 expected to quit for good.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Some statistics of the campaign include: (a) an estimated 1.64 million Americans tried to quit smoking because of the 2012 campaign; (b) approximately 100,000 smokers are expected to quit for good; (c) an estimated six million non-smokers talked with friends and family about the dangers of smoking; and (d) an estimated 4.7 million additional non-smokers recommended cessation services to their friends and family.

sections.label: Smoking rate reduction plateauing
sections.summary: The rate of reduction of smoking rates is plateauing and smoking among the young remains stubbornly high.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The rate of reduction of smoking rates is plateauing and the rate of smoking amongst the young is still stubbornly high.

sections.label: Point-of-sale tobacco promotion exposure
sections.summary: Children and adolescents exposed to point-of-sale tobacco promotion had higher odds of trying smoking and being susceptible to future smoking.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The evidence was clear: children and adolescents who were exposed to point-of-sale tobacco promotion have around 1.6 times higher odds of having tried smoking and around 1.3 times higher odds of being susceptible to future smoking, compared with those who were less frequently exposed.

sections.label: Raising minimum smoking age to 21
sections.summary: The speaker feels 18 is still too young and calls for the minimum age to be raised to at least 21.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I think this has also been brought up by some of the hon Members who have spoken before me.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I also feel that 18 is still too young and would like to call for it to be raised to at least 21 years of age.

sections.label: Plain packaging for tobacco products
sections.summary: Since point-of-sale displays are already banned, the speaker feels introducing plain packaging for tobacco products would be an incremental but significant move.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Second, since we are already banning point-of-sale displays, I feel that it would just be an incremental but still significant move if we were to continue with our plans to introduce plain packaging for tobacco products.

sections.label: Support for TCASA amendment
sections.summary: The speaker warmly supports the TCASA amendment as a step towards a tobacco-free generation and safeguarding society's health.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Dr Lisa Henriksen from the Stanford Prevention Research Centre of Stanford University recently wrote of the retail environment as a barometer of progress towards the endgame for tobacco control.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: And I strongly believe that this amendment to the TCASA is an important step towards safeguarding the health of our society and it is an important step towards a tobacco-free generation and so I warmly support it.

sections.label: Specialist tobacconists outlets
sections.summary: There are about 17 specialist tobacconists, and five outlets belong to the same company.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Presently, there are about 17 such specialist tobacconists – in fact, five of the outlets are from the same company.

sections.label: Point-of-sale display ban retailers
sections.summary: The point-of-sale display ban will not be implemented at Changi Airport duty-free retailers for now, but seaport duty-free retailers must comply.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Given this, the point-of-sale display ban will not be implemented at duty-free retailers at Changi Airport for now, although we will continue to review the position.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Duty-free retailers at seaports will be required to comply with the point-of-sale display ban.

sections.label: One-year grace period
sections.summary: A grace period of one year is considered reasonable.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: As such, we think a grace period of one year is reasonable.

sections.label: Cohort ban not pursued
sections.summary: MOH will not pursue a cohort ban for now because enforcing it can be very challenging.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Furthermore, enforcing such a cohort ban can be very challenging as age differences between close cohorts become less apparent physically as they grow into adults.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Hence, MOH will not pursue such a cohort ban for now.

sections.label: Minimum legal age consultation
sections.summary: Raising the minimum legal age is still being studied in a public consultation due to end on 29 March 2016.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: We are still studying raising the minimum legal age as part of the on-going public consultation on further amendments of our tobacco control measures, which include standardised packaging and larger graphic health warnings.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: This public consultation is due to end on 29 March 2016.

sections.label: Campaign sign-ups
sections.summary: The campaign has seen about 10,000 sign-ups each year since 2014.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: The campaign has seen about 10,000 sign-ups each year since 2014.

sections.label: Doubling number nationwide by 2020
sections.summary: By 2020, the aim is to double the number to 600 nationwide.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: By 2020, the aim is to double the number to 600 nationwide.

sections.label: Prohibition on online advertising
sections.summary: Singapore will make clear its prohibition on advertising covers online advertising and promotion from Singapore or Singapore-connected persons.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Regardless of developments elsewhere, we will play our part as a responsible member of the global public health community by making it clear that our prohibition on advertising will cover online advertising and promotion that originate from Singapore or from Singapore-connected persons.

sections.label: No warrant required for search powers
sections.summary: The amendments clarify no warrant is required for authorised officers to search premises and vehicles on reasonable suspicion before evidence is disposed of.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: The amendments simply clarify that no warrant is required to exercise such powers because authorised officers need to be able to act on reasonable suspicion and in a timely manner to search premises and vehicles for evidence in connection with a possible offence, before the suspect can dispose of the evidence.

sections.label: Studying Project DSP and ENDS measures
sections.summary: MEWR and NEA are studying Project DSP's progress, and regulatory measures need strengthening amid ENDS popularity and targeted marketing to youths.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: MEWR and NEA are currently studying the progress of Project DSP: Cool to be Considerate, to gauge the public's response to these DSPs.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: With the recent increase in the popularity of Electronic Nicotine Delivery System (ENDS) worldwide and their targeted marketing to youths, we need to strengthen our regulatory measures.
